ds: Financial footprints of the purchase, sale or live-streaming of child sexual abuse material and related exploitation. Indicators are limited to payment patterns and account behaviour so that institutions can file reports promptly; staff must never access, view or retain the material and should escalate to specialist teams and law enforcement.

FATF and APG, Financial Flows from Human Trafficking (2018)
WeProtect Global Alliance, Global Threat Assessment (2023 edition; earlier 2019, 2021)
UNODC and ECPAT public material on online child sexual exploitation

cn.rt: Small recurring payments to individuals or sites by card or fast payment from personal accounts.

rat: Small recurring payments to individuals or sites; wallets, crypto, remittance.

ind.n: Repeated low-value payments to overseas recipients with live-stream links
ind.cx: Small recurring transfers to individuals in jurisdictions of known high-risk, with references to live shows or streaming.
ind.fp: Remittances to family and creator payments are common.
ind.ds: Small recurring transfers to individuals in jurisdictions of known high-risk, with references to live shows or streaming.

ind.n: Payments to platforms flagged for illegal content
ind.cx: Payments to websites, hosting or payment accounts identified in intelligence as selling abuse material.
ind.fp: Domain intelligence can include false matches.
ind.ds: Payments to websites, hosting or payment accounts identified in intelligence as selling abuse material.

ind.n: Crypto transfers to addresses linked to abuse marketplaces
ind.cx: Customer sends virtual assets to wallets clustered with abuse-related services.
ind.ds: Customer sends virtual assets to wallets clustered with abuse-related services.

ind.n: Pattern of many small payments from many accounts to one recipient
ind.cx: Facilitator receives many micro-payments from unrelated senders.
ind.fp: Content creators receive many small tips.
ind.ds: Numerous unrelated payers send frequent, often small, payments to one account, wallet or beneficiary, or one funder pays many beneficiaries, with no clear commercial relationship.
ind.cn: Many unrelated senders paying a single account or recipient

ind.n: Customer receiving payments for access to minors
ind.cx: Account shows payments in return for introductions or access, plus use of prepaid cards and anonymous payment methods.
ind.fp: Unrelated legitimate activity can resemble these flows.
ind.ds: Account shows payments in return for introductions or access, plus use of prepaid cards and anonymous payment methods.

ind.n: Use of multiple payment apps and e-wallets with different names
ind.cx: Same user holds several e-wallets under various identities, funded with cash vouchers.
ind.ds: The same individual appears under different names or opens several accounts or wallets, directly or through an intermediary.
ind.cn: One person holding multiple identities or accounts

ind.n: Requests for payments to be hidden or descriptions disguised
ind.cx: Customer uses deceptive references or asks to avoid records on payments.
ind.ds: Customer uses deceptive references or asks to avoid records on payments.

ind.n: Payments from or to persons with prior convictions or adverse media relating to child exploitation
ind.cx: Customer appears in credible reports or sanctions of offences against children.
ind.fp: Records may be old or mismatched.
ind.ds: Credible negative news, enforcement notices or investigations link the customer, its owners or associates to criminal, corrupt or regulated-sector misconduct.
ind.cn: Adverse media on customer or associates

ctl.ds: Screens payment instructions, references and narrative fields for restricted parties, goods, places and concealment language using tuned matching logic. It catches exposure that does not appear in the customer record.

ctl.n: Specialist investigation and suspicious activity reporting
ctl.ds: Trained analysts investigate alerts with typology playbooks, document rationale and file reports where suspicion is formed, with prompt reporting to the competent authority. It converts alerts into actionable intelligence.

Monitors merchant-level patterns such as ticket size, refund, void and chargeback rates, descriptor mismatch and cross-merchant flows. It identifies transaction laundering, bust-out and illicit merchants.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.
Traces exposure of deposit and withdrawal addresses to illicit clusters and screens wallets with risk-scored alerts. It reveals on-chain exposure.

ctl.n: Fan-in, fan-out and funnel account detection
ctl.ds: Detects accounts receiving from many unrelated senders, or sending to many beneficiaries, followed by consolidation or onward movement. It surfaces collector, funnel and mule structures.

Monitors specialised products such as insurance, securities, safe deposit and prepaid instruments for surrender, free delivery, overpayment, assignment, matched trades and unusual access. It catches product-specific abuse.

Provides discreet escalation routes and private conversation procedures so staff can refer suspected victims of exploitation, coercion or trafficking to specialists, police and support organisations. It prioritises victim safety.

Remote verification of a person's identity using document capture, biometric matching and liveness or anti-spoofing checks, or a trusted digital identity. It reduces impersonation, synthetic identities and account opening with stolen or fabricated credentials.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.
Provides a simple internal reporting channel and feedback loop so front-line staff can escalate observations, pressure and cash-handling anomalies. It turns staff observations into cases for review.

Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.
